newsitem.title: UK: Thistle Hotels float put at 1.05-1.24 billion stg.
newsitem.headline: Thistle Hotels float put at 1.05-1.24 billion stg.

text.p: UK hotels group Thistle Hotels Plc said on Wednesday the offer price in its flotation is expected to be between 170 and 210 pence per share.
The price values Thistle, Britain's second largest hotel group, at betweeen 1.05 billion and 1.24 billion stg.
The offer will leave New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd, which currently holds 70 percent of the company, with less than 50 percent.
The float will comprise new shares plus the sale of 17 percent of the existing shares and will total around 402 million stg, Thistle said in its offer prospectus.
Thistle forecast operating profit before exceptional items for its 1996 financial year of not less than 100 million stg, with pro forma earnings per share of not less than 10.31 pence.
Pro forma gearing as at July 14 1996 would have been 32.7 percent.
Had the shares been listed for the whole of the current financial year, Thistle said it would have paid a total dividend of 3.7p, representing a yield of 2.4 percent.
Aside from Brierley, the current shareholders in Thistle are two investment arms of the Singapore government.
Announcement of the offer price and basis of share allocations is due on October 2, when conditional dealings in the shares are expected to start.
There are three tranches -- a UK offer which involves placings with insitutions and an offer to retail investors through intermediaries, a U.S. offer and an international offer.
Individual shareholders will be entitled to join a club which will offer discounts and other benefits at Thistle hotels and restaurants.
